rationale: Meeting frequency of the Central Advisory Board; not an accessibility deadline.
Power to amend the Schedule; not an accessibility deadline.
Measures for cultural and recreational participation; no time limit for buildings.
Meeting frequency of State Advisory Boards; not an accessibility deadline.
Existing public buildings must be made accessible within five years of the accessibility rules, with extensions and action plans.
Service providers must meet accessibility rules within two years; the companion time limit for services rather than buildings.
Vacancy returns to special employment exchanges; not sign language.
Agreements for audio-visual workers; unrelated.
Toll free helpline for migrant workers; unrelated.
Government must ensure access to electronic media through sign language interpretation, close captioning and accessible formats.
Inclusive education measures include employing teachers qualified in sign language; a related obligation in the education setting.
Penalty for disclosing complaint contents; not compensation to the woman.
Lists the factors the Committee weighs in fixing compensation to the aggrieved woman: trauma, lost career opportunity, medical expenses, respondent's means and mode of payment.
On a proved allegation the Committee recommends deducting a sum from the respondent's salary for the aggrieved woman, recoverable as land revenue; the companion procedure.
Punishes knowing use of an infringing computer programme; a computer-related offence in another Act, not unauthorised access.
Obstruction of OSH inspectors; unrelated.
Child sexual abuse material offence; not hacking.
Punishes penetrating or accessing a computer resource without authorisation when done with terrorist intent or to obtain restricted data; an aggravated hacking offence, not the general one.
Section 66 (punishment for computer related offences, i.e. acts in section 43 done dishonestly or fraudulently) is the direct answer but is not admitted.
Section 43 (penalty and compensation for unauthorised access to a computer system) is a direct answer but is not admitted.
Copyright exists only under the Act; not image-based offences.
Bars releasing photographs of mental health patients to media without consent; a narrow confidentiality rule, not an offence for intimate images.
Processing of children's personal data; not image offences.
Grounds for processing personal data; consent in a data-processing sense, not an image offence.
Free consent in contracts; same word, different sense.
Cross-border transfer of personal data; unrelated.
Punishes publishing or transmitting sexually explicit material electronically; covers sharing but not non-consensual capture, so 2 rather than 3.
Punishes publishing obscene electronic material generally; torn between 1 and 2 as it is broader than intimate images, so the lower.
Section 66E (punishment for capturing or publishing images of a person's private area without consent) is the direct answer but is not admitted.
Courts' cognizance of RERA offences; not the tribunal.
Adjudicating officer decides compensation claims; a first-level body, not the appellate tribunal.
Establishes the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal and lets anyone aggrieved by the Authority or adjudicating officer appeal to it.
Procedure and sixty-day limit for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal; the companion procedure.
Ship owner may apply to fix the limit of liability for bunker oil pollution; a companion procedure on oil pollution liability.
General limitation of maritime claims that expressly excludes oil pollution claims; only cross-refers.
Contribution between vessels for personal injury damages; not oil pollution.
Bars enforcing pollution claims against other property once the limitation fund is set up; a companion rule on compensation.
Ship owner is liable for pollution damage caused by the ship in an incident, subject to listed defences, with claims channelled through this Chapter.
Persons suffering pollution damage may claim compensation from the established fund; the companion claims procedure.
International Fund pays where full compensation cannot be had under the Civil Liability Convention; supplementary compensation.
Welfare facilities like washing and canteens; not leave.
Contractor's responsibility to pay wages; not leave.
Repeal and savings; not leave.
Journey allowance for migrant workers; a different benefit.
Audio-visual worker agreements; not a leave entitlement.
Notice of commencement of operations; unrelated.
Workers with 180 days' work in a year earn one day's leave with wages per twenty days, with carry-forward and encashment.
Paid annual leave for seafarers under a different Act; similar topic but a different workforce.
